title: Kids Go Free Offers: Where Children Get In Free
description: Where kids get in free: age rules at theme parks, under-5s free at heritage sites, Blue Peter badges, free museums and how to check an offer.
h1: Kids go free: where children get in for nothing
intro: With a few kids in tow, ticket prices add up fast. The good news: lots of places let children in free, if you know the rules. Here’s where to look.

image.alt: Two parents holding a toddler’s hands on a sunny walk

cardText: Age rules, badges and schemes that let children in free.

blocks.title: Scout’s free-for-kids rule
blocks.text: Always check the age rule on the official site: “under 3” and “3 and under” aren’t the same thing, and some free child tickets still have to be booked.
points: Bring proof of age for older kids if asked
Free tickets may still need reserving
One offer per ticket is the norm

sections.html:
• Disney: under-3s go free at Disneyland Paris, Walt Disney World and Disneyland Resort.
  • LEGOLAND and other Merlin parks: under-3s are typically free.
  • Warner Bros. Studio Tour London: children aged 4 and under go free with a ticket.
The National Trust and English Heritage both let under-5s in free at most properties. See which membership suits you.

• Blue Peter badge holders get free entry at 200+ UK attractions.
  • US fourth graders get a free Every Kid Outdoors pass for the family.
  • French national museums admit under-18s free.
National museums in the UK and the Smithsonian in Washington DC are free for everyone. See our free days out guide.

faqs.q: Do under-3s go free at theme parks?
faqs.a: At most major parks, yes, including Disney parks and LEGOLAND. Always check the park’s own ticket rules.

faqs.q: Do free child tickets need booking?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Many attractions with timed entry ask you to reserve a free ticket for babies and toddlers so they can manage capacity.
